title.es: Cómo empaquetan ideas los textos académicos

es: Reconocer cómo un verbo o un adjetivo se convierte en sustantivo (nominalización) para compactar información en un texto académico.

teaching.en: The rapid growth of cities has put pressure on housing.
teaching.es: El rápido crecimiento de las ciudades ha presionado la vivienda.
teaching.explanationEs: «Cities have grown rapidly» se empaqueta: el verbo grow pasa a growth y el adverbio rapidly pasa a adjetivo (rapid).
segments: The rapid growth of cities
has put pressure on housing.
teaching.audioText: The rapid growth of cities has put pressure on housing.

teaching.en: The adoption of the new method improved the assessment of student work.
teaching.es: La adopción del nuevo método mejoró la evaluación del trabajo de los estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: Dos verbos (adopt, assess) se vuelven sustantivos: en lugar de acciones, son «cosas» de las que se puede hablar.
segments: The adoption of the new method
improved the assessment of student work.
teaching.audioText: The adoption of the new method improved the assessment of student work.

teaching.en: Greater awareness of the risk led to a significant reduction in accidents.
teaching.es: Una mayor conciencia del riesgo llevó a una reducción significativa de los accidentes.
teaching.explanationEs: «People became aware and accidents fell» se comprime: aware → awareness, fell → reduction; significant indica el grado.
segments: Greater awareness of the risk led
to a significant reduction in accidents.
teaching.audioText: Greater awareness of the risk led to a significant reduction in accidents.

teaching.en: The efficiency of the system depends on regular checks.
teaching.es: La eficiencia del sistema depende de revisiones periódicas.
teaching.explanationEs: El adjetivo efficient pasa a efficiency (-ent → -ency); el grupo nominal entero es el sujeto de depends.
segments: The efficiency of the system
depends on regular checks.
teaching.audioText: The efficiency of the system depends on regular checks.

teaching.en: Rapid growth is not always good news for a small business.
teaching.es: El crecimiento rápido no siempre es una buena noticia para un pequeño negocio.
teaching.explanationEs: Sin of, growth también funciona como sustantivo pleno: «Rapid growth» es el sujeto de la frase.
segments: Rapid growth is not always good
news for a small business.
teaching.audioText: Rapid growth is not always good news for a small business.

prompt.es: Elige la versión nominalizada de «Cities grew rapidly».

choices.text: The rapidly grow of cities
The rapid growth of cities
The growth rapid of cities

feedback.es: Growth es el sustantivo de grow, rapid (adjetivo) va delante y el sujeto original pasa tras of.

hint.es: El verbo se vuelve sustantivo y el adverbio pasa a adjetivo delante de él.

prompt.es: Completa: «La adopción del nuevo sistema redujo los errores.»

answer.text: adoption

feedback.es: Adoption es el sustantivo del verbo adopt y funciona como sujeto de reduced.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo de adopt: termina en -ion.

origin.text: The ___ of the new system reduced errors.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La investigación del accidente llevó semanas.»

answer.text: The investigation of the accident took weeks

feedback.es: El sujeto es el grupo nominal The investigation of the accident; took es el verbo principal.

hint.es: Empieza por el grupo nominal «The investigation», que hace de sujeto.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada grupo nominal con la idea verbal que contiene.

pairs.es: La gente es más consciente del riesgo
El servicio es eficiente
Los costes se redujeron de forma significativa

pairs: the fair assessment of the essays

pairs.es: Se evaluaron los ensayos con justicia
La atención mejoró

feedback.es: Cada sustantivo guarda un verbo o adjetivo escondido: awareness (aware), efficiency (efficient), reduction (reduce), assessment (assess), improvement (improve).

pairs.es: La gente es más consciente del riesgo
El servicio es eficiente

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ocurrió con el experimento.

choices.text: It worked perfectly, and the team was proud.
It was postponed, and the team was worried.
It did not work, and the team was surprised.

feedback.es: Failure viene de fail: el experimento falló y eso sorprendió al equipo.

origin.audio: The failure of the experiment surprised the whole team.

prompt.es: Completa: «El desarrollo del proyecto fue lento.»

answer.text: development

feedback.es: Development es el sustantivo de develop y hace de sujeto de was slow.

origin.text: The ___ of the project was slow.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase nominalizada resume la oración del texto?

choices.text: A large increase in sales allowed the company to take on more staff.
A large decrease in sales allowed the company to take on more staff.
A large increase in sales forced the company to take on fewer staff.

feedback.es: Increase es el sustantivo de «increased» y mantiene el sentido; las otras frases cambian el significado.

origin.text: Sales increased a lot, so the company took on more staff.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué problema describe la hablante.

choices.text: There are fewer students, so classrooms are empty.
There are more students than classrooms.
The classrooms were closed after a fire.

feedback.es: Growth in the number of students equivale a «the number of students grew»; shortage indica que faltan aulas.

origin.audio: Rapid growth in the number of students caused a shortage of classrooms.

prompt.es: Completa: «La decisión de cerrar la tienda fue difícil.»

answer.text: decision

feedback.es: Decision es el sustantivo de decide y hace de sujeto, seguido de to + verbo.

origin.text: The ___ to close the shop was difficult.

prompt.es: Escribe el grupo nominal equivalente; empieza con «The rapid…».

answer.text: The rapid development of the product
accepted: The rapid development of the product
The rapid development of the new product
The rapid development of this product

feedback.es: Develop pasa a development, el adverbio rapidly pasa a adjetivo rapid y el objeto va tras of.

origin.text: They developed the product rapidly.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La escasez de agua preocupa a todos.»

answer.text: The shortage of water worries everyone

feedback.es: The shortage of water es un grupo nominal que hace de sujeto de worries.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase contiene una nominalización hecha a partir de un adjetivo?

choices.text: The data were collected carefully.
They collected the data last year.
The reliability of the data is high.

feedback.es: Reliability viene del adjetivo reliable; en las otras frases la información sigue en verbos.

prompt.es: Una de estas frases está mal formada. ¿Cuál es?

choices.text: The growth rapid of the company surprised us.
The rapid growth of the company surprised us.
The company's rapid growth surprised us.

feedback.es: El adjetivo rapid debe ir antes de growth; las otras dos colocan bien el adjetivo.

es: Usar adjetivos evaluativos académicos (robust, flawed, compelling, tentative) para valorar un estudio con su razón, y reconocer la pasiva impersonal.

teaching.en: The results are robust because the sample was large and the method was clear.
teaching.es: Los resultados son sólidos porque la muestra fue grande y el método era claro.
teaching.explanationEs: Robust valora que un resultado resiste aunque cambien las condiciones; se justifica con because.
segments: The results are robust because the sample
was large and the method was clear.
teaching.audioText: The results are robust because the sample was large and the method was clear.

teaching.en: The study is flawed: its sample was too small to support any conclusion.
teaching.es: El estudio tiene fallos: su muestra era demasiado pequeña para sostener una conclusión.
teaching.explanationEs: Flawed señala un defecto de diseño; los dos puntos introducen la razón.
segments: The study is flawed: its sample was
too small to support any conclusion.
teaching.audioText: The study is flawed: its sample was too small to support any conclusion.

teaching.en: The evidence for the claim is compelling, since three teams found the same effect.
teaching.es: La evidencia de la afirmación es convincente, ya que tres equipos encontraron el mismo efecto.
teaching.explanationEs: Compelling significa que la evidencia convence; since da la razón.
segments: The evidence for the claim is compelling,
since three teams found the same effect.
teaching.audioText: The evidence for the claim is compelling, since three teams found the same effect.

teaching.en: The authors remain tentative about their findings, so more research is needed.
teaching.es: Los autores siguen siendo cautelosos con sus hallazgos, así que hace falta más investigación.
teaching.explanationEs: Tentative indica que el autor no se compromete: sus conclusiones son provisionales.
segments: The authors remain tentative about their
findings, so more research is needed.
teaching.audioText: The authors remain tentative about their findings, so more research is needed.

teaching.en: It is widely believed that coffee improves memory, but the proof is not conclusive.
teaching.es: Se cree ampliamente que el café mejora la memoria, pero la prueba no es concluyente.
teaching.explanationEs: Repaso de la pasiva impersonal (It is believed that…); conclusive significa que la cuestión queda cerrada.
segments: It is widely believed that coffee improves
memory, but the proof is not conclusive.
teaching.audioText: It is widely believed that coffee improves memory, but the proof is not conclusive.

teaching.en: The survey was thorough, but its questionable wording may have influenced the answers.
teaching.es: La encuesta fue minuciosa, pero su redacción dudosa pudo influir en las respuestas.
teaching.explanationEs: Thorough valora el cuidado del trabajo; questionable señala algo en lo que no se puede confiar del todo.
segments: The survey was thorough, but its questionable
wording may have influenced the answers.
teaching.audioText: The survey was thorough, but its questionable wording may have influenced the answers.

prompt.es: Completa: «El estudio tiene fallos porque la muestra estaba sesgada.»

answer.text: flawed

feedback.es: Flawed es el adjetivo que señala un defecto de diseño, aquí el sesgo de la muestra.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de flaw: algo que tiene un defecto.

origin.text: The study is ___ because the sample was biased.

prompt.es: Los autores no quieren comprometerse con sus datos. ¿Qué frase refleja esa cautela?

choices.text: Our conclusions are conclusive.
Our conclusions are thorough.
Our conclusions are tentative.

feedback.es: Tentative indica que el autor considera sus conclusiones provisionales.

hint.es: Busca el adjetivo que significa provisional.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La evidencia es convincente porque tres equipos coincidieron.»

answer.text: The evidence is compelling because three teams agreed

feedback.es: Compelling califica la evidencia y because añade la razón.

hint.es: Después de The evidence va is y el adjetivo evaluativo.

prompt.es: Completa cada valoración con el adjetivo de la lista que mejor encaje.

answer.text: flawed | robust | compelling | tentative

feedback.es: Cada razón pide un adjetivo: sesgo → flawed; se repite siempre → robust; difícil no estar de acuerdo → compelling; solo un primer vistazo → tentative.

The same effect appeared in every test and in every country, so the result is ___.

origin.text: Words: robust · flawed · compelling · tentative

prompt.es: Un estudio tiene solo quince participantes. ¿Qué valoración es la más cautelosa?

choices.text: The results are tentative and need more research.
The results prove the theory.
The results are conclusive for everyone.

feedback.es: Con una muestra pequeña lo prudente es llamar tentative a los resultados; las otras afirman demasiado.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la hablante del estudio.

choices.text: The study is flawed because it was too short.
The work was careful, but some questions may have biased the answers.
The evidence is conclusive, and she trusts it.

feedback.es: Thorough elogia el método, pero questionable dice que las preguntas no son fiables del todo.

origin.audio: I read the whole paper. The method is thorough, but the survey questions are questionable, so I would not trust the results yet.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se dice que el desayuno mejora las notas; la prueba no es concluyente.»

answer.text: conclusive

feedback.es: Conclusive significa que la cuestión queda cerrada; aquí la prueba no basta para cerrarla.

origin.text: It is often said that breakfast improves grades, but the proof is not ___.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase valora con justicia un estudio pequeño pero bien hecho?

choices.text: The study is flawed, so its results are compelling.
The study is conclusive because it was small.
The study is thorough, but its small sample makes the results tentative.

feedback.es: Se elogia el cuidado (thorough) y se modera el resultado (tentative); las otras frases se contradicen.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué confía la hablante en la conclusión.

choices.text: Because several teams repeated the experiment with the same result.
Because the authors say the conclusion is only provisional.
Because the sample was small but very careful.

feedback.es: La hablante justifica compelling con la repetición del resultado por cuatro equipos.

origin.audio: Their conclusion is compelling. Four teams repeated the experiment and all four got the same result.

prompt.es: Valora el estudio en una frase: resultado sólido, muestra grande y autores cautos.

answer.text: The results are robust because the sample was large, but the authors remain tentative.
accepted: The results are robust because the sample was large, but the authors remain tentative.
The findings are robust since the sample was large, but the authors are still cautious.
The result is robust because 3000 people took part, although the authors remain tentative.

feedback.es: Una buena valoración califica el resultado, da la razón (muestra grande) y recoge la prudencia de los autores.

origin.text: Un estudio con 3000 participantes de cinco países en el que el mismo resultado aparece siempre; aun así, los autores son muy prudentes.

answer.text: The study is flawed and its sample is questionable

feedback.es: Flawed y questionable señalan dos debilidades distintas: el diseño y la muestra.

prompt.es: Un compañero dice que un resultado es «robust». ¿Qué quiere decir?

choices.text: The result is only provisional.
The result holds up in different tests.
The result has a serious weakness.

feedback.es: Robust significa que el resultado se mantiene en distintas pruebas; provisional sería tentative y con fallos, flawed.

provisional, sin compromiso

title.es: Leer un resumen de estudio a toda velocidad

es: Leer un abstract y extraer objetivo, método, resultado y postura del autor, distinguiendo una inferencia justificada de una exagerada.

teaching.en: The aim of this study was to examine whether later start times improve sleep.
teaching.es: El objetivo de este estudio era examinar si una hora de inicio más tardía mejora el sueño.
teaching.explanationEs: El abstract empieza por el aim: qué pregunta quiere responder, normalmente con whether y en pasado.
segments: The aim of this study was to
examine whether later start times improve sleep.
teaching.audioText: The aim of this study was to examine whether later start times improve sleep.

teaching.en: We followed 240 adolescents in four schools for one year.
teaching.es: Seguimos a 240 adolescentes en cuatro colegios durante un año.
teaching.explanationEs: El método dice quién participó, cuántos fueron y cuánto duró; aquí el dato es 240 y un año.
segments: We followed 240 adolescents in
four schools for one year.
teaching.audioText: We followed 240 adolescents in four schools for one year.

teaching.en: Adolescents at the later schools slept about fifty minutes longer.
teaching.es: Los adolescentes de los colegios con inicio más tardío durmieron unos cincuenta minutos más.
teaching.explanationEs: Los resultados traen cifras y comparaciones (longer): es lo que se midió, sin opinión.
segments: Adolescents at the later schools
slept about fifty minutes longer.
teaching.audioText: Adolescents at the later schools slept about fifty minutes longer.

teaching.en: These findings suggest that later start times may benefit adolescents.
teaching.es: Estos hallazgos sugieren que una hora de inicio más tardía puede beneficiar a los adolescentes.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest + may es una postura cautelosa: el autor no afirma que el beneficio esté demostrado.
segments: These findings suggest that later
start times may benefit adolescents.
teaching.audioText: These findings suggest that later start times may benefit adolescents.

teaching.en: Further research is needed before schools change their timetables.
teaching.es: Hace falta más investigación antes de que los colegios cambien sus horarios.
teaching.explanationEs: La última frase suele marcar un límite del estudio y dónde debe seguir la investigación.
segments: Further research is needed before
schools change their timetables.
teaching.audioText: Further research is needed before schools change their timetables.

teaching.en: The authors' stance is cautious: they write «may», not «will».
teaching.es: La postura de los autores es cauta: escriben «may» y no «will».
teaching.explanationEs: La postura (stance) se lee en los verbos y modales: may, suggest = cautela; will, prove = seguridad.
segments: The authors' stance is cautious:
they write «may», not «will».
teaching.audioText: The authors' stance is cautious: they write «may», not «will».

prompt.es: ¿En qué campo del abstract aparece «We followed 240 students for one year»?

choices.text: Method
Aim
Conclusion

feedback.es: Dice quién participó, cuántos fueron y cuánto duró: eso describe el método.

hint.es: Responde a quién participó y durante cuánto tiempo.

prompt.es: Completa: «El objetivo de este estudio era examinar si el ruido afecta a la memoria.»

answer.text: aim

feedback.es: Aim es el objetivo: abre el abstract y formula la pregunta del estudio.

hint.es: Es la palabra para «objetivo»; tiene tres letras.

origin.text: The ___ of this study was to examine whether noise affects memory.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Estos resultados sugieren que puede haber un beneficio.»

answer.text: These findings suggest that there may be a benefit

feedback.es: Suggest + may expresa una conclusión cauta.

hint.es: Después de suggest va that y luego la oración con may.

prompt.es: Lee el abstract y completa los cuatro campos con sus datos.

answer.text: later start times | 240 | fifty | may

feedback.es: Cada dato sale de un campo: objetivo (later start times), método (240), resultado (fifty) y postura cauta (may).

sentences: Aim: to examine whether ___ improve sleep and attention.
Method: ___ students were followed in four schools for one year.
Result: students at the later schools slept about ___ minutes longer.
Stance: the authors say later start times ___ benefit adolescents.
origin.text: Aim: This study examined whether starting school later improves the sleep and attention of adolescents. Method: We followed 240 students in four schools for one year. Two schools moved the start of the day to 9:00; the other two did not. Results: Students at the later schools slept about fifty minutes longer each night and reported better attention in class. Conclusion: Although the sample came from a single city, these findings suggest that later start times may benefit adolescents. Further research is needed.

prompt.es: ¿Qué inferencia está justificada por el abstract?

choices.text: All teenagers will improve their grades if school starts later.
Later start times may help adolescents sleep longer.
Sleeping longer makes students pay less attention.

feedback.es: Los autores solo sugieren que puede ayudar a dormir más; las otras frases afirman más o lo contrario de lo que miden.

origin.text: Aim: This study examined whether starting school later improves the sleep and attention of adolescents. Method: We followed 240 students in four schools for one year. Two schools moved the start of the day to 9:00; the other two did not. Results: Students at the later schools slept about fifty minutes longer each night and reported better attention in class. Conclusion: Although the sample came from a single city, these findings suggest that later start times may benefit adolescents. Further research is needed.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué resultado presenta el abstract.

choices.text: App users remembered fewer words than the others.
Both groups remembered the same number of words.
App users remembered more words, but only slightly.

feedback.es: El resultado es un pequeño aumento: «remembered more words, but the gain was small».

origin.audio: This study asked whether apps help people learn words. We tested two hundred adults for six weeks. Those who used the app remembered more words, but the gain was small.

prompt.es: Una de estas inferencias exagera lo que dice el abstract. ¿Cuál?

choices.text: Less homework will reduce stress in every school in every country.
Less homework may reduce stress without lowering grades.
The survey found no change in grades.

feedback.es: El abstract solo sugiere (may) un efecto en diez colegios; «will… in every school» generaliza sin datos.

origin.text: Aim: This study asked whether less homework reduces stress in adolescents. Method: We surveyed 500 students in ten schools; half of the schools reduced homework to thirty minutes a night. Results: Students with less homework reported lower stress, but their grades did not change. Conclusion: The findings suggest that less homework may reduce stress without harming grades, although the answers came from the students themselves.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hace falta más investigación antes de estar seguros.»

answer.text: Further

feedback.es: Further research is needed es la fórmula con la que un abstract marca sus límites.

origin.text: ___ research is needed before we can be sure.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué son cautos los autores.

choices.text: Because the runners refused to sleep longer.
Because they studied only a small group.
Because the injuries were serious.

feedback.es: Los autores explican su cautela con la muestra: «Because the sample was small, we remain tentative».

origin.audio: We followed sixty runners for one year. Those who slept longer had fewer injuries. Because the sample was small, we remain tentative.

prompt.es: Resume el abstract en dos frases: objetivo, resultado y postura del autor.

accepted: The study examined whether less homework reduces stress in adolescents. Students with less homework reported lower stress, and the authors suggest that it may help without harming grades.
The aim was to examine whether less homework reduces stress. Students with less homework reported less stress, and the authors suggest that it might help while grades stayed the same.

feedback.es: Un buen resumen recoge el objetivo, el resultado principal y la postura cauta (suggest, may).

origin.text: Aim: This study asked whether less homework reduces stress in adolescents. Method: We surveyed 500 students in ten schools; half of the schools reduced homework to thirty minutes a night. Results: Students with less homework reported lower stress, but their grades did not change. Conclusion: The findings suggest that less homework may reduce stress without harming grades, although the answers came from the students themselves.

answer.text: The authors say further research is needed before drawing conclusions
accepted: The authors say further research is needed before drawing conclusions
The authors say that further research is needed before drawing conclusions

feedback.es: Further research is needed es la fórmula típica con que un abstract marca sus límites.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del autor es más cautelosa?

choices.text: Our results prove a clear benefit.
Our results show that everyone benefits.
Our results suggest a small benefit.

feedback.es: Suggest y small mantienen la cautela; prove y everyone afirman demasiado.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada campo del abstract con la pregunta que responde.

pairs.es: Qué pregunta quiere responder el estudio
Quién participó y cómo se midió
Qué datos se obtuvieron
Qué significan los datos y qué límites tienen

feedback.es: Cada campo responde a una pregunta distinta y siempre aparecen en ese orden.

es: Parafrasear un párrafo atribuyendo las ideas con verbos de cita adecuados (argue, claim, maintain, acknowledge, according to) y condensándolo con una nominalización.

teaching.en: It is not enough to change a few words when you paraphrase a source.
teaching.es: No basta con cambiar unas palabras cuando parafraseas una fuente.
teaching.explanationEs: Parafrasear es decir lo mismo con otra estructura y otras palabras; cambiar solo sinónimos sigue siendo copiar.
segments: It is not enough to change a
few words when you paraphrase a source.
teaching.audioText: It is not enough to change a few words when you paraphrase a source.

teaching.en: According to the report, bicycle use has tripled in five years.
teaching.es: Según el informe, el uso de la bicicleta se ha triplicado en cinco años.
teaching.explanationEs: According to atribuye la idea a una fuente de forma neutral; después va una oración completa, sin that.
segments: According to the report, bicycle use
has tripled in five years.
teaching.audioText: According to the report, bicycle use has tripled in five years.

teaching.en: Some critics claim that the data for small shops are incomplete.
teaching.es: Algunos críticos afirman que los datos de los comercios pequeños están incompletos.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim toma distancia: quien escribe no se compromete con lo que afirma la fuente.
segments: Some critics claim that the data
for small shops are incomplete.
teaching.audioText: Some critics claim that the data for small shops are incomplete.

teaching.en: The authors argue that the investment pays for itself.
teaching.es: Los autores sostienen que la inversión se paga sola.
teaching.explanationEs: Argue presenta una tesis que la fuente defiende con razones; va seguido de that.
segments: The authors argue that the
investment pays for itself.
teaching.audioText: The authors argue that the investment pays for itself.

teaching.en: Many planners maintain that safer streets attract more customers.
teaching.es: Muchos urbanistas sostienen que las calles más seguras atraen a más clientes.
teaching.explanationEs: Maintain expresa una convicción firme y mantenida en el tiempo.
segments: Many planners maintain that safer
streets attract more customers.
teaching.audioText: Many planners maintain that safer streets attract more customers.

teaching.en: The authors acknowledge that their sample was small.
teaching.es: Los autores reconocen que su muestra era pequeña.
teaching.explanationEs: Acknowledge introduce una limitación que la propia fuente admite.
segments: The authors acknowledge that
their sample was small.
teaching.audioText: The authors acknowledge that their sample was small.

prompt.es: Quieres dejar claro que tú dudas de lo que afirma la fuente. ¿Qué frase usas?

choices.text: Some critics acknowledge that the plan is cheap.
Some critics claim that the plan is cheap.
Some critics maintain that the plan is cheap.

feedback.es: Claim toma distancia; acknowledge admite que es cierto y maintain lo defiende con firmeza.

hint.es: Este verbo se usa cuando quien escribe no se compromete con la idea.

prompt.es: Completa: «Según el informe, el uso de la bici se triplicó.»

answer.text: According

feedback.es: According to introduce la fuente de forma neutral.

hint.es: Va seguido de to y significa «según».

origin.text: ___ to the report, bicycle use tripled.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los autores reconocen que la encuesta era limitada.»

answer.text: According to the study, the new bike lanes have led to a rapid growth in cycling and a reduction in car traffic. The lead researcher argues that the investment has already paid for itself, and she points out that shop sales along the lanes have risen. accepted: According to the study, the new bike lanes have led to a rapid growth in cycling and a reduction in car traffic. The lead researcher argues that the investment has already paid for itself, and she points out that shop sales along the lanes have risen. Critics claim, however, that the results for small shops are unreliable. She acknowledges this limitation and suggests repeating the survey with a larger sample.

The study shows a rise in cycling and a decrease in traffic after the city built bike lanes. The researcher maintains that the project has paid for itself, and she notes that shops along the lanes sell more. Some critics claim that the information about small businesses is incomplete, and she acknowledges that a larger survey is needed next year.

feedback.es: Una buena paráfrasis atribuye con dos verbos distintos, condensa con una nominalización y conserva las ideas clave con otras palabras.

origin.text: Five years ago, the city council decided to build more than one hundred kilometres of protected bike lanes. At first, many residents were against the plan. Shop owners were especially worried, because they believed that fewer parking places would mean fewer customers. However, the figures published this spring tell a different story. The number of people who cycle to work has risen from three per cent to eleven per cent, and car traffic in the centre has fallen by nine per cent. Air quality has also improved, and the noise in the main streets has decreased. Several schools have reported that more pupils now come to class by bicycle. The researcher who led the study argues that the investment has already paid for itself, because the city now spends less on road repairs and on health care. She points out that sales in the shops along the new lanes have grown by six per cent. Nevertheless, some critics claim that the results for small shops are unreliable, since only forty businesses answered the survey. The researcher acknowledges this limitation, and she suggests that the council should repeat the survey next year with a larger sample.

title.en: Summarise a study for the study group
title.es: Resumir un estudio para el grupo de estudio

es: Resumir un estudio sencillo ante el grupo con registro académico: objetivo, método, resultado, una pasiva impersonal y una respuesta prudente a una duda.

teaching.en: It is widely assumed that teenagers need more sleep than adults.
teaching.es: Se da por sentado que los adolescentes necesitan dormir más que los adultos.
teaching.explanationEs: Pasiva impersonal: It is + participio + that + oración; presenta una opinión general sin decir quién la sostiene.
segments: It is widely assumed that teenagers
need more sleep than adults.
teaching.audioText: It is widely assumed that teenagers need more sleep than adults.

teaching.en: It has been shown that later start times improve attention.
teaching.es: Se ha demostrado que una hora de inicio más tardía mejora la atención.
teaching.explanationEs: Con el presente perfecto se escribe It has been shown (con been): es un resultado ya establecido.
segments: It has been shown that
later start times improve attention.
teaching.audioText: It has been shown that later start times improve attention.

prompt.es: Resume el estudio: objetivo, método, resultado, pasiva impersonal y respuesta cauta.

answer.text: The aim of this study was to examine whether daily walking improves memory. Briefly, two hundred adults were followed for six weeks, and half of them walked thirty minutes a day. Overall, the people who walked scored eight per cent higher on a memory test. It is often assumed that exercise helps memory, and these findings suggest a modest benefit. However, all the participants were volunteers, so it is difficult to generalise the results to everyone. To answer your question, we cannot say that exercise improves memory for all people. Further research is needed, and for now the conclusion is tentative.
accepted: The aim of this study was to examine whether daily walking improves memory. Briefly, two hundred adults were followed for six weeks, and half of them walked thirty minutes a day. Overall, the people who walked scored eight per cent higher on a memory test. It is often assumed that exercise helps memory, and these findings suggest a modest benefit. However, all the participants were volunteers, so it is difficult to generalise the results to everyone. To answer your question, we cannot say that exercise improves memory for all people. Further research is needed, and for now the conclusion is tentative.

This study examined whether walking every day improves memory. Two hundred adults took part for six weeks, and half of them walked for thirty minutes a day. The people who walked scored 8% higher in a memory test. It is believed that exercise helps memory, and the findings suggest a small benefit. However, the participants were all volunteers, so we cannot say that the result applies to everyone. To answer your question, it is difficult to generalise from this group. Further research is needed, so the conclusion is tentative.

feedback.es: Un buen resumen recorre objetivo, método y resultado, incluye una pasiva impersonal y responde con cautela al límite de la muestra.

origin.text: Estudio: ¿caminar cada día mejora la memoria? 200 adultos durante seis semanas; la mitad caminó 30 minutos al día. Los que caminaron puntuaron un 8 % más en una prueba de memoria. Un compañero pregunta: «¿Podemos asegurar que el ejercicio mejora la memoria?» Escribe el resumen (objetivo, método y resultado), usa una pasiva impersonal y responde con cautela.
